item.research_question: What is the influence of a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure on the formation of magnetic vortex states and the origin of coercivity in AlCo(Cr)FeNi high-entropy alloys?
item.processing_route: Arc melting of Al, Co, Cr, Fe, and Ni pellets in an Ar atmosphere, followed by annealing at 600°C for 15 h in an Ar atmosphere and quenching in water
item.test_conditions: Bulk magnetization measured at 300 K up to 1 T; Lorentz TEM and off-axis electron holography performed in magnetic-field-free conditions and with applied out-of-plane fields up to 1.5 T; APT conducted at 60 K
key_findings: AlCoFeNi has a saturation magnetization (MS) of 99.8 Am2/kg and coercivity (Hc) of 1.45 mT, while AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi has MS of 46.2 Am2/kg and Hc of 9.56 mT.
AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi exhibits a hierarchical structure with coarse A2 gen-1 (1–5 μm), medium A2 gen-2 (50-150 nm), and fine A2 gen-3 (<10 nm) phases in a B2 matrix.
A2 gen-2 precipitates in region R1 contain 3D magnetic vortex states with a magnetic induction peak of 0.5 ± 0.1 T.
The ratio of clockwise to counterclockwise magnetic vortices in A2 gen-2 precipitates is approximately 1:1 at remanence.
The A2 shell surrounding A2 gen-2 precipitates is 2 nm thick and has ~25% higher magnetization than the A2 gen-1 matrix in region R2.
Magnetic vortices in A2 gen-2 precipitates can reverse their rotation direction when exposed to external magnetic fields of 100–500 mT.
The B2 matrix in region R1 is weakly ferromagnetic and reverses its magnetization sign during magnetic switching.
item.mechanism: The increased coercivity in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi is attributed to a complex magnetization process involving the successive reversal of magnetic vortices within A2 precipitates and interactions with a weakly ferromagnetic B2 matrix, rather than simple domain wall pinning.
item.limitations: The interactions between different magnetic elements remain unclear; off-axis electron holography cannot detect the magnetic vortex core direction; the study does not cover the effects of temperature, strain, or magnetic field on precipitate formation.
item.future_work: Future studies should determine the effect of external magnetic field and/or stress annealing, kinetics, and other external stimuli on precipitate formation to control magnetic anisotropy and properties; in situ magnetizing experiments and micromagnetic simulations are needed to address dynamic reversal processes.
quotes: We reveal for the first time the influence of a hierarchically decomposed B2 + A2 structure in an AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi HEA on the formation of magnetic vortex states within individual A2 (disordered BCC) precipitates.
The switching behavior of the magnetic microstructure is related to soft magnetism.

The increased coercivity of the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi HEA, which remains in the soft ferromagnetic range, can be attributed to a complicated magnetization reversal process, which involves the reversal of magnetic vortices in a weakly ferromagnetic matrix.
